title: Paging ZIdentity lists: offset and limit, the list envelope, and how each SDK walks pages
aliases: zidentity list only returns first page

prose.text: ZIdentity lists page by offset and limit rather than by page number. {{offset-limit}}

prose.label: The envelope.
prose.text: {{envelope-required}} {{next-link-string}} The contract and both SDKs disagree on whether that envelope arrives as an object or inside an array {{divergence:list-response-shape}}. No source gives the page size the API uses when `limit` is omitted {{gap:default-page-size}}.

prose.label: Go.
prose.text: {{go-walk}} {{go-limit-clamp}} The Go name lookups page the same way and filter on the client: [[zidentity.sdk-go:getbyname-client-side]].

prose.label: Python.
prose.text: {{python-single-page}} {{python-next}} {{python-empty-next-link}} What the last page carries in `next_link` is open {{gap:last-page-next-link}}. The paging fields on the Python list objects themselves come back empty: [[zidentity.sdk-python:envelope-meta-lost]].

checks.do: Whether a Python caller pages at all: a `list_*` call returns one page, so a count that stops at the first page's size points at a missing loop.
Whether a Python loop over `has_next()` ends, by checking what `next_link` the last page returns.
Whether a Go caller's limit was silently ignored because it was outside 1 to 1000.

offset-limit.statement: List operations take `offset`, the number of records to skip (minimum 0), and `limit`, the records returned per request (minimum 0, maximum 1000).

envelope-required.statement: A list response object carries `results_total`, `pageOffset`, `pageSize`, `next_link`, `prev_link` and `records`, all marked required; the paging keys mix snake_case and camelCase.

next-link-string.statement: `next_link` is typed as a string: the URL of the next page of records, if available.

expect.description: URL link to the next page of resource servers, if available. Helps to navigate through paginated results.

go-walk.statement: The Go SDK's list helper `ReadAllPagesWithPagination` requests 100 records per page when the caller passes no parameters, stops at the first page shorter than the limit or with an empty `NextLink`, advances the offset by the number of records received, and applies any JMESPath filter only after collecting every page.

go-limit-clamp.statement: The Go parameter builder turns a page size of 0 or less into 100 and caps one above 1000 at 1000; `WithLimit` keeps the previous limit when given a value outside 1 to 1000, and `WithOffset` ignores a negative offset, both without an error.

python-single-page.statement: The Python SDK's `list_users`, `list_groups`, `list_api_clients` and `list_resource_servers` each execute one request and wrap that one response body in a typed object (`Users`, `Groups`, `APIClients`, `ResourceServers`).

python-next.statement: For ZIdentity responses the Python response object keeps the body's `records` and `next_link`; `has_next()` is true whenever `next_link` is not None, and `next()` copies the query string of `next_link` into the request parameters, points the request at `next_link`'s scheme, host and path, and sends a GET.

quotes: # ZIAM (ZIdentity Admin) uses "records" field for paginated responses
self._params[key] = value[0] if len(value) == 1 else value

python-empty-next-link.statement: If the last page carries `next_link` as an empty string rather than omitting it, Python's `has_next()` stays true and `next()` repeats the request for the same page, so a loop that runs while `has_next()` never ends; the Go helper treats an empty `next_link` as the end.
python-empty-next-link.conditions: Conditional on the last-page value of `next_link`, which no source shows; the contract's marking it as a required string makes an empty string plausible but does not show it. `next()` changes the URL only when `next_link` is non-empty.

list-response-shape.summary: The contract types every list (and get-by-ID) 200 response as an array whose items are the envelope, while both SDKs decode a single envelope object.

positions.says: GET /users returns an array of objects, each carrying the paging fields and `records`.

quotes: The endpoint answers with a bare JSON array rather than
paginated envelope the rest of this package uses, so there is no page

positions.says: List endpoints answer with one paginated envelope object, which Go decodes into `PaginationResponse`; the secrets list is the exception that answers a bare array.

quotes: # ZIAM (ZIdentity Admin) uses "records" field for paginated responses

positions.says: Python reads `records` and the paging keys from a ZIdentity body that is an object.

list-response-shape.impact: A client generated from the contract would expect a top-level array for lists and single reads and fail to decode what the SDKs decode; hand-written callers should follow the SDKs' object envelope until a capture shows otherwise.

default-page-size.title: How many records a ZIdentity list returns when `limit` is omitted
default-page-size.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the default page size is 100 and the maximum 1000. The maximum is in the contract; 100 is only the Go SDK's own default. The contract gives no server default, and a Python `list_*` call without `limit` returns whatever that default is as its only page.
default-page-size.blocks: telling whether a Python list result is complete

last-page-next-link.title: What `next_link` holds on the last page of a ZIdentity list
last-page-next-link.detail: Unverified legacy statement: an empty string in `next_link` signals the last page. The contract marks `next_link` as a required string but no source shows a last page; whether it is empty, null or absent decides whether Python's `has_next()` loop terminates.
last-page-next-link.blocks: relying on the Python response object's `next()` to read a whole list
